articles.title: Pix of the Day, 30 September, 2026 - Across the world
articles.summary: Burkina Faso has inaugurated its first gold refinery as its military-led government seeks to strengthen economic sovereignty after breaking ties with its traditional Western partners. “From now on, Burkina Faso’s gold must not only be mined in Burkina Faso; it must also be processed, controlled, valued and certified there,” President Ibrahim Traoré said on Monday at the inauguration of the refinery, named Raffinor-BF.

articles.title: Burkina Faso Opens First Gold Refinery
articles.summary: Burkina Faso has opened its first gold refinery as the military-led government seeks greater control over the country's mineral wealth and to reduce its reliance on exporting raw materials. The Raffinor-BF facility in Ouagadougou cost more than $19 million and has a refining capacity of 164 tonnes of gold per year, with plans to eventually increase capacity to 515 tonnes.

articles.title: Burkina Faso opens first gold refinery in push for economic independence
articles.summary: Burkina Faso opened its first gold refinery on Monday, pushing ahead with plans to better organise the commercialisation of the precious metal in one of the continent's top producers. The west African nation is the continent's third leading gold producer, churning out more than 94 tonnes of the precious metal last year, according to the World Gold Council. But authorities traditionally struggle to control the informal gold mining sector, which has been blighted by jihadist violence and smuggling.

articles.title: 7 Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso Launches First Gold Refinery
articles.summary: According to a statement by the Burkina Faso government's Information Service, Mr Traore said Burkina Faso has "reached a historic milestone in its quest for economic independence." Burkina Faso has launched its first gold refinery, the RAFFINOR-BF refinery, with the primary aim of processing its mineral resources domestically. The country's military leader, Ibrahim Traore, inaugurated the refinery in Ouagadougou on Monday.

articles.title: Burkina Faso launches first gold refinery
articles.summary: Burkina Faso has launched its first gold refinery, the RAFFINOR-BF refinery, with the primary aim of processing its mineral resources domestically. The country’s military leader, Ibrahim Traore, inaugurated the refinery in Ouagadougou on Monday. He described the refinery as a part of the administration’s plan to cut dependence on primary exports.

articles.title: Crash of the Ouagadougou-Alger flight: Swiftair condemned
articles.summary: The families of the victims had to wait twelve years. Gathered within the association "AH-5017 Ensemble", they led a "relentless fight for truth and justice" which is now experiencing its judicial outcome. The Spanish company Swiftair is found guilty of manslaughter this Monday morning by the Paris Criminal Court .

articles.title: Niger: what we know about the jihadist attack that targeted Niamey airport
articles.summary: Niger: what we know about the jihadist attack that targeted the Niamey airport Published on Saturday, January 31, 2026 | AFP In the night from Wednesday to Thursday, the Niamey airport in Niger suffered a brief attack claimed Friday by the Islamic State, in a country where jihadist violence usually occurs in the west and south-east The Nigerien military junta, helped by "Russian partners", accused the French, Beninese and Ivorian presidents of being the "sponsors" of the attackers, words condemned by Abidjan and Cotonou on Friday.

articles.title: Niger: Islamic State claims responsibility for attack on Niamey airport
articles.summary: Published on Friday, January 30, 2026 | AFP The Islamic State claimed responsibility on Friday for the attack on Niamey airport in Niger, said the Site group, which specializes in counter-terrorism research . On the night of Wednesday to Thursday, Niamey airport, which is home to military sites and is about ten kilometers from the presidency, was the target of an attack leaving 20 dead on the attacking side, according to the Nigerien military junta .

articles.title: Niger: A Significant Quantity of Cocaine Worth More Than 2.5 Billion FCFA Seized in Agadez
articles.summary: Niger: A large quantity of cocaine worth more than 2.5 billion FCFA seized in Agadez This is a hard blow for drug traffickers in Niger. The country's national gendarmerie caught three individuals carrying a significant amount of cocaine. The events took place on September 14, about fifteen kilometers from the village of RTA (Agadez region) .

articles.title: Fight against drugs: 50 kg of cocaine worth 2.5 billion CFA seized in Agadez
articles.summary: The defence and security forces of the Agadez region in northern Niger have just carried out a nice operation to seize a large quantity of hard drugs. It is, in fact, more than 50 kg of pure cocaine, with an estimated value of more than 2.5 billion CFA, which were intercepted by elements of the National Gendarmerie, who also seized other narcotic products during a security operation conducted in the department of Arlit, in the same region, on the Algerian border.

articles.title: After the abortive coup d 'état, Niger joined the anti-Emirate axis
articles.summary: The failed coup attempt of 28 August at Niamey airport shifted Niger to the side of Algeria in the anti-United Arab Emirates axis. By Nathalie Prevost A telephone conversation with General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan a week ago, followed, two days later, by an audience with the Sudanese ambassador to Niger . General Abdourahamane Tiani embraces the maxim of international relations: "the enemies of my enemies are my friends".

articles.title: Air Force: Colonel Alka Mahaman Sani now in command of Niamey Air Base 101
articles.summary: The Chief of Staff of the Air Force, Air Brigadier General Salifou MAINASSARA, chaired, Friday, September 17, at Air Base 101 in Niamey, the handover ceremony between the Commander of the outgoing base, Air Brigadier General Sidi Oumar KA ISMAEL KA, and incoming, Colonel ALKA Mamane Sani . Commander of base 201 in Agadez since 2024, the new boss of the most important and strategic air base of the Nigerien forces is an officer specializing in aeronautics and military air transport.

articles.title: Attempted destabilization: an ESA delegation in Niamey to mark the solidarity of the Confederation in Niger
articles.summary: This Friday, September 18, 2026, a delegation from the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), composed of Burkinabe and Malian ministers in charge of Defence and Foreign Affairs, was received in Niamey by the President of the Republic, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani . The meeting was an opportunity for the delegation to express the solidarity of Burkina Faso and Mali in Niger, after the destabilization attempt that occurred on the night of 28 to 29 August 2026, and to offer its condolences to the families of the victims .
